the rotational diffusion coefficient of ribosomes can be determined from depolarized laser-light scattering and that the rotational diffusion constant of ribosome is 2.3 x 10(-6) sec(-1) at 20 degrees C.

the rotational diffusion coefficient of ribosome is determined from the depolarization light scattering spectrum measured in photon correlation spectroscopy and the rotational diffusion coefficient obtained is consistent with the non-spherical shape of the ribosome.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for measuring the rotational diffusion coefficient of biological particles and its application to the ribosome.

a determination of rotational and translational diffusion coefficients of the ribosome from depolarized and polarized laser light scattering, respectively, using the technique of photon correlation spectroscopy.
the development of the theory for depolarized light-scattering spectra of non-spherical macromolecules, and the application of this theory to obtain the rotational diffusion coefficient of ribosomes.

the rotational and translational diffusion coefficients can be measured from the same sample, and therefore, the hydrodynamic radius can be determined with greater accuracy.
